title: Ops cadence syncplay and hallway asks
content:
Purpose
- Short working doc to align leadership rehearsal, cascade notes, and the \"hallway asks\" list for the upcoming company forum and the Q2 OKR roll. This lives as a lightweight prep sheet we can iterate in the 72 hours before the all-team meeting.

Top-level outcomes we want after the forum
1) People know the 3 cross-company priorities for the quarter and the observable signals we will measure.
2) Engineering teams understand the desired latency/cost SLO adjustments and where to escalate tradeoffs.
3) Two clear asks for product and sales to carry forward into customer conversations.
4) A short list of decisions (or decision owners) to close within 14 days post-forum.

Agenda (30–40m total, tight)
- 0–3m: Welcome + 1-sentence reminder of mission (CEO)
- 3–8m: Quick health snapshot (metrics slide): latency P50/P95 trend, cost per 1M tokens, infra availability (SRE)
- 8–18m: Three priority narratives (each 3m): Host, Dedicated, Private — focus on user impact and expected asks of engineers and GTM
- 18–25m: OKR highlights (product leads, 90s each) — show 3 objective-level outcomes and top 3 KR changes
- 25–33m: Cross-team rollouts and canary/fallback plan (platform + SRE)
- 33–38m: Open Q&A (moderated, surfaced top 6 pre-submitted + 2 live)
- 38–40m: Close + concrete next steps and who owns what

Rehearsal notes (for execs)
- Keep narratives metric-led: tie each priority to 1 metric we track in Console (latency P95, cost per inference, adoption by top 5 customers).
- Avoid deep technical digressions — send follow-up deep dives to product channels.
- Have an explicit fallback line: \"If we cannot meet the latency target in region X, we will prioritize routing and temporary instance scaling for critical customers.\"
- Practice the 30-second hand-off between CEO -> Head of Product -> Head of Engineering.

Hallway asks (what people will ask in passing after the meeting)
- \"How will this affect my sprint?\" -> propose: add a single ticket per team to capture any infra/exec ask; product ops will triage daily for 7d.
- \"Are we adding new quotas or rate limits?\" -> answer: not globally; targeted experiments for high-traffic routes only.
- \"Will my team need to rescope features for quantization?\" -> answer: only if specifically called out in the KR; we will provide a 2-week optimize playbook and a quantization checklist.
- \"How to get early access to Dedicated capacity?\" -> link to Dedicated intake form (post-meeting) and SE contact list.

OKR thread (draft language for cascade)
- Objective A: Make inference reliable and predictable for product teams.
  - KR1: Reduce platform-induced P95 inference latency by 15% for standard routes.
  - KR2: Cut per-token serving cost by 12% on average for our three most common models.
  - KR3: Ship a fallback routing policy with region-aware defaults and documented SLOs.

- Objective B: Reduce time-to-onboard for Dedicated/Private customers.
  - KR1: Cut average provisioning time for Dedicated pools to 48 hours.
  - KR2: Create a 1-click VPC onboarding checklist and 3 validation tests.
  - KR3: Pilot Private deployment with 2 regulated customers and publish compliance learnings.

- Objective C: Developer experience and observability improvements.
  - KR1: Release token-level cost breakdown in Console and raise adoption to 60% of active teams.
  - KR2: Ship tracing hooks for 3 client SDKs.
  - KR3: Publish 10 runbooks for common regression classes (e.g., perf regressions, model divergence).

Cascade guidance (one-pager language to send to managers)
- Keep team OKRs to maximum 3 objectives.
- Map each team KR back to one company KR where possible (link in the OKR spreadsheet).
- Add a single engineering ask ticket if work impacts infra priorities; label as \"ops-cascade-urgent\" for 14-day triage.

Decision log (things we need to decide within 14 days)
- Whether to adopt regional auto-scaling thresholds as default (owner: SRE).
- Finalize Dedicated capacity pricing floor for Q2 (owner: Finance + Product).
- Approve the fallback routing policy (owner: Platform).

Open questions (to be surfaced in pre-forum surveys)
- What constitutes a \"critical\" customer for auto-burst approvals? (ops + sales input required)
- Should we accelerate the quantized model catalog for non-enterprise routes? (product/engineering tradeoff)
- Which SDK should get tracing-first integration in the first quarter?

Prep checklist (who does what in next 72 hours)
- Deck updates: metrics slide (SRE), priority narratives (CEO + Product), OKR bullets (product leads) — due in 48h.
- Rehearsal slot: book 30m with execs + 1 moderator (Avery) — done by 24h.
- Triage pre-submitted questions (Riley + Samira) — collect by 48h.
- Post-meeting artifacts: short FAQ doc + Dedicated intake link + follow-up survey (product ops) — draft in 24h, publish within 6h of meeting close.

Comms snippets (short copy for internal post)
- Headline: \"This quarter: predictable inference performance, faster Dedicated onboarding, and clearer observability for every team.\"
- Call to action: \"If your work will touch infra SLA, add an \"ops-cascade-urgent\" ticket this week or ping product-ops.\"

Notes to self
- Keep tone optimistic + realistic. Don’t promise immediate big cost drops — talk about incremental wins and measurable experiments.
- Collect 2–3 customer blurbs from Solutions by EOD Wednesday to include in the narrative.
- Post meeting: run a 15m sync with platform leads to confirm triage queue for incoming tickets.

Appendix: quick links (to paste into meeting chat)
- Dedicated intake: https://forms.gd/dedicated-intake-placeholder
- OKR spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/OKR-2025-Q2
- Fallback policy draft: CONFLUENCE-ORG/FALLBACK-2025

---
Status: draft — please add short comments in-line. This doc is intentionally concise so execs can skim and managers can copy/paste the cascade guidance."
